title: GPU unit tests fail with a burst of 37 gtest-parallel worker crashes right after fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch
signature: GPU unit tests accuracy tolerance mismatch in fusion test (val_ref vs val_opt difference exceeds tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp) followed by burst of concurrent gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with code 3|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 accuracy mismatch (diff 3.05e-05 > tolerance 1e-05), immediately followed by 36 more tests (mostly convolution_random_smoke_test and fusings_gpu cases) exiting with code 3 and GPU clFinish CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES errors

key_errors:
fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance, where
val_ref[i] evaluates to -0.04473876953125,
val_opt[i] evaluates to -0.044769287109375, and
tolerance evaluates to 9.9999997473787516e-06.
[  FAILED  ] fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1

fusion_test_common.hpp(87): error: Expected: val_opt = get_output_values_to_float(fused, outputs_fused.begin()->second) doesn't throw an exception.
  Actual: it throws ov::Exception with description "Exception from openvino\src\plugins\intel_gpu\src\runtime\ocl\ocl_stream.cpp:421:
[GPU] clFinish, error code: -5 CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES"
root_cause: The first test (fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1) fails on a borderline floating-point accuracy mismatch (3.05e-05 vs a 1e-05 tolerance) comparing fused vs. non-fused GPU kernel outputs - a known tight-tolerance flake on this Windows iGPU runner. Immediately afterward, 36 more gtest-parallel worker processes (running convolution and fusion tests in parallel) start failing with GPU runtime exception 'clFinish, error code: -5 CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES', indicating the GPU/OpenCL driver ran out of resources under the concurrent parallel test load on the shared Windows iGPU runner. This is the same recurring pattern already tracked in the post-commit pattern database (signature_hash 502c01bffd8f35db), now observed for the 6th time across unrelated commits, strongly indicating a runner-level resource exhaustion issue triggered by gtest-parallel concurrency on iGPU rather than a code regression introduced by this specific commit.
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible outside the CI Windows iGPU runner. Locally: build ov_gpu_unit_tests, run with gtest_parallel.py at similar worker concurrency against an Intel iGPU device, and repeat fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 and nearby convolution_random_smoke_test cases many times; CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES is more likely to reproduce under concurrent load on constrained GPU memory/compute resources.
recommended_actions: Investigate reducing gtest-parallel worker concurrency for GPU unit tests on Windows iGPU runners to avoid CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES under concurrent kernel execution.
Review/relax the fusion accuracy tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp for fp16_scale_out-style comparisons, or adjust the reference computation to reduce the fp16/fp32 rounding gap.

Escalate to the iGPU CI runner pool owners: this is the 6th occurrence of the same signature in ~24h; consider temporarily marking affected convolution/fusion tests as known-flaky or capping test parallelism until root-caused.
Add retry-on-failure for CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES specifically in gtest-parallel GPU test runs to avoid blocking post-commit merges on transient runner resource exhaustion.
prevention_strategies: Add CI-level detection that treats a cluster of CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES failures immediately following an accuracy-tolerance failure as a known runner-resource-exhaustion signature, auto-retrying the GPU unit test job once before failing the pipeline. Track GPU resource utilization/memory pressure metrics during gtest-parallel runs to correlate with worker concurrency.
historical_context: This exact signature (502c01bffd8f35db) has recurred 5 times in roughly the last 24 hours across unrelated commits (runs 43369335165, 43398624960, 43430895182, 43440149471, 43461440649), always starting with the same fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch followed by a burst of CL_OUT_OF_RESOURCES worker crashes. This run is the 6th occurrence, confirming it is a persistent runner/infrastructure-level flake rather than an isolated incident.
